stem: A team is picking compute for two jobs: an occasional SQL query over log files already sitting in S3, and an existing Spark job they want to run without provisioning or sizing a cluster. Which TWO compute options fit these two jobs respectively? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Amazon Athena for the occasional SQL query
Amazon EMR in cluster mode for the occasional SQL query
Amazon EMR Serverless for the existing Spark job
An Amazon S3 access point for the existing Spark job
AWS Lake Formation for the occasional SQL query

rationale: Athena runs the occasional ad hoc SQL query directly against the log files in S3 with nothing to provision, and EMR Serverless runs the existing Spark job on the same open-source framework without provisioning or sizing a cluster. Running EMR in cluster mode for an occasional query means standing up and paying for a persistent cluster for infrequent work, more infrastructure than the job needs. An S3 access point only scopes network and permission access to a bucket; it has no compute capability to run a Spark job at all. Lake Formation manages catalog permissions, it does not execute SQL queries itself.
